validity.recommendation: No action on existence/duplicate/classification for P2352 itself. It is the genuine, physically distinct Phase I segment of the Power of Siberia system (Chayandinskoye NGKM, Sakha Republic -> Blagoveshchensk, Amur Oblast, ~2,200 km, operating since Dec 2, 2019) and is clearly distinguishable from its named-family siblings on the 32-pipeline roster: P2353 is Phase II (Kovyktinskoye field, Irkutsk Oblast -> Chayandinskoye NGKM, ~800-803.5 km, commissioned Dec 21, 2022 per Gazprom's own 2022 Annual Report -- see cross_row_leads); P3208 appears, per an independent technical-library phase breakdown (neftegaz.ru), to correspond to a Phase III COMPRESSOR-STATION-ONLY capacity expansion along the SAME already-existing Chayandinskoye-to-Atamanskaya section of THIS segment's own corridor (7 new compressor stations, 481 MW, targeted for 2022) -- i.e. likely no new physical pipe of its own (flagged as a cross_row_lead for P3208's own audit, not resolved here, since it bears on P3208's LengthKnown/Diameter fields, not P2352's); P5521 (Belogorsk-Khabarovsk) and any Power-of-Siberia-2/'Sila Baikala' rows are later, physically separate, not-yet-complete corridors connecting the Power of Siberia system to the unrelated Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok system (RBC 2024: construction just beginning on Belogorsk-Khabarovsk, targeted for 2029) and must not be confused with P3208's compressor work. No indication P2352 duplicates, or is duplicated by, any other roster row.
